skills.label: Modal verbs: can, should, must, have to

form: *can / should / must* + base verb: *I can swim. You should rest. He must go.*
No *-s* with *he / she / it*: *he can, she should, it must.*
Negative: *can't* (*cannot*), *shouldn't*, *mustn't* + base verb. Question: *Can / Should / Must* + subject + base verb?
*have to* is a normal verb: *she has to go.* Negative and questions with *do / does*: *I don't have to go. Do you have to go?*
use: *can*: ability (*I can swim*) and permission (*Can I sit here?*).
*should*: advice (*You should see a doctor*).
*must / have to*: it is necessary, a rule or a duty (*You must wear a seat belt. I have to wear a uniform at work*). Often both are possible.
*mustn't* = not allowed. *don't have to* = not necessary (*You mustn't park here. You don't have to pay*).

*must* has no past form for obligation: use *had to* (*I had to work late*). In the future we often say *will have to* (*We will have to leave early*), but *must* can also point to the future (*You must call me tomorrow*).
rule.signals: *rule, law, allowed, necessary, advice, ability*
rule.example: *You must wear a seat belt, but you don't have to wear a hat.*
watch: Never *to* after *can / should / must*: *I can go* (not *I can to go*).
No *will can*: *I will be able to come.*
*can* in the past: *could*: *I could swim when I was five.*
Requests: *Could you…?* is more polite than *Can you…?*
*Must I…?* sounds formal; *Do I have to…?* is more common.

form: *can / should / must* + darbības vārda pamatforma: *I can swim.* *You should rest.* *He must go.*
Nav *-s* ar *he / she / it*: *he can, she should, it must*.
Noliegums: *can't* (*cannot*), *shouldn't, mustn't* + pamatforma. Jautājums: *Can / Should / Must* + teik. priekšmets + pamatforma?
*have to* ir *parasts* darbības vārds: *she has to go*. Noliegums un jautājums ar *do / does*: *I don't have to go.* *Do you have to go?*
use: *can*: spēja (*I can swim*) un atļauja (*Can I sit here*?).
*should*: padoms (*You should see a doctor*).
*must / have to*: tas ir nepieciešams, *noteikums* vai pienākums (*You must wear a seat belt.* *I have to wear a uniform at work*). Bieži der abi.
*mustn't = aizliegts*. *don't have to* = nav obligāti (*You mustn't park here.* *You don't have to pay*).

*must* nav pagātnes formas pienākumam: lieto *had to* (*I had to work late*). Nākotnē bieži lieto *will have to* (*We will have to leave early*), bet *must* var norādīt arī uz nākotni (*You must call me tomorrow*).
rule_lv.signals: *rule, law, allowed, necessary, advice, ability* (*noteikums, likums*, atļauts, nepieciešams, padoms, spēja)
watch: Nekad to aiz *can / should / must*: *I can go* (nevis *I can to go*).
Nav *will can*: *I will be able to come.*
*can* pagātnē: *could*: *I could swim when I was five.*
Lūgumi: *Could you*…? ir pieklājīgāk nekā *Can you*…?
*Must I*…? izklausās oficiāli; biežāk saka *Do I have to*…?

skills.label: Comparison: -er, more, the most, as ... as

form: *Short adjectives*: adjective + *-er* + *than* (*Rachel is taller than Tom*). Superlative: *the* + adjective + *-est* (*the tallest*).
Spelling: *big - bigger - the biggest*; *nice - nicer - the nicest*; *heavy - heavier - the heaviest*.

Most one-syllable adjectives and many two-syllable adjectives ending in *-y* take *-er / -est* (*heavier, the heaviest*). Most longer adjectives, and many other two-syllable ones, take *more / the most* (*more expensive than, the most expensive*). Some allow both.
Irregular: *good - better - the best*; *bad - worse - the worst*; *far - further - the furthest*.
*as* + adjective + *as* = equal (*My phone is as fast as yours*). *not as ... as* = less (*This bag is not as heavy as that one*).
use: Comparative: compare two things or people. Superlative: one thing compared with all the others in a group (*the tallest student in the class*).
After a superlative we use *in* + place or group: *the biggest city in the country*.
*the same as, similar to, different from*: *It is the same colour as mine.*
*much / a lot / a bit / slightly* + comparative says how big the difference is (*much cheaper, a bit colder*). *less ... than* and *the least* say the opposite of *more ... than* and *the most*.
rule.signals: *than, as ... as, the ... -est, in, much, a bit, the same as*
rule.example: *This bike is cheaper than that one, but it is not as fast as mine.*
watch: *than me / than him* in everyday English: *She's taller than me.*
Never both: *bigger* (not *more bigger*), *the best* (not *the most best*).
*the* + comparative, *the* + comparative: *The sooner, the better.*
*fun* is an exception: *more fun* (not *funner*). *clever, quiet* take *-er* or *more*.
*as ... as* with the same adjective: *as tall as* (not *so tall as* or *as tall like*).

form: Īsie īpašības vārdi: īpašības vārds + *-er + than* (*Rachel is taller than Tom*). Vispārākā pakāpe: *the* + īpašības vārds + *-est* (*the tallest*).
Pareizrakstība: *big - bigger - the biggest; nice - nicer - the nicest; heavy - heavier - the heaviest*.

Lielākā daļa *vienzilbes* īpašības vārdu un *daudzi divzilbju* vārdi ar *-y galotni* lieto *-er / -est* (*heavier, the heaviest*). Lielākā daļa garāku vārdu, kā arī *daudzi citi divzilbju* vārdi lieto *more / the most* (*more expensive than, the most expensive*). Daži der ar *abiem*.
Neregulārie: *good - better - the best; bad - worse - the worst; far - further - the furthest*.
*as* + īpašības vārds + *as* = vienāds (*My phone is as fast as yours*). *not as* ... *as* = mazāk (*This bag is not as heavy as that one*).
use: Pārākā pakāpe: salīdzina divus cilvēkus vai *lietas*. Vispārākā pakāpe: *viens* salīdzināts ar *visiem* pārējiem grupā (*the tallest student in the class*).
Aiz vispārākās pakāpes lieto *in + vieta* vai *grupa*: *the biggest city in the country*.
*the same as, similar to, different from*: *It is the same colour as mine.*
*much / a lot / a bit / slightly* + pārākā pakāpe parāda, cik *liela* ir atšķirība (*much cheaper, a bit colder*). *less* ... *than* un *the least* ir pretējs *more* ... *than* un *the most*.
rule_lv.signals: *than, as* ... *as, the* ... *-est, in, much, a bit, the same as* (nekā, *tikpat* ... kā, visā, *daudz, mazliet*, tāds *pats* kā)
watch: *than + me / him* sarunā: *She's taller than me.*
Nekad *abus* kopā: *bigger* (nevis *more bigger*), *the best* (nevis *the most best*).
*the + comparative, the + comparative*: *The sooner, the better.*
*fun* ir izņēmums: *more fun* (nevis *funner*); *clever, quiet* var gan ar *-er*, gan ar *more*.
*as* ... *as* ar to pašu īpašības vārdu: *as tall as* (nevis *so tall as* vai *as tall like*). *Latviski tikpat* garš kā, tāpēc *rodas like*.

form: *If* + present simple, present simple: *If you heat ice, it melts.*
You can use *when* or *whenever* instead of *if*: *Whenever it rains, the road gets slippery.*
Negative: *If you don't water plants, they die.*
use: Facts that are always true (science, nature).
General rules and habits.
Instructions: *If the light is red, stop.*
rule.signals: *if, when, whenever, every time*
rule.example: *If you leave biscuits on the desk, someone eats them.*
watch: *if* and *when* mean almost the same here: *If / When you mix red and blue, you get purple.*
Present simple in both parts, not *will*: *If you press this, the door opens* (not *If you will press this, the door opens*).
A comma after the *if*-part when it comes first: *If it rains, the road gets wet.* No comma when it comes second: *The road gets wet if it rains.*
The second part can be an instruction: *If you feel sick, stay at home.*

form: *If* + Present Simple, Present Simple: *If you heat ice, it melts.*
Var lietot arī *when* vai *whenever*: *Whenever it rains, the road gets slippery.*
Noliegums: *If you don't water plants, they die.*
use: Vienmēr patiesi fakti (zinātne, daba).
Vispārīgi noteikumi un ieradumi.
Norādījumi: *If the light is red, stop.*
rule_lv.signals: *if, when, whenever, every time*
watch: *if* un *when* šeit nozīmē gandrīz to pašu: *If / When you mix red and blue, you get purple.*
Abās daļās Present Simple, nevis *will*: *If you press this, the door opens* (nevis *If you will press this, the door opens*).
Ja *if* daļa ir pirmā, aiz tās liek komatu: *If it rains, the road gets wet.* Ja otrā, *komata* nav: *The road gets wet if it rains.*
Otrā daļa var būt pavēle: *If you feel sick, stay at home.*

form: *If* + present simple, *will* + base verb: *If it rains, we will stay home.*
The if-part can come second: *We will stay home if it rains.*
Other modals are possible in the result: *may, might, can, should.*
No *will* after *if*: *If it rains* (not *If it will rain*).
use: Real, possible situations in the future.
Promises, warnings and offers.
First conditional = one future situation. Zero conditional = always true.
rule.signals: *if, unless, as soon as, when, in case*
rule.example: *If you send the email now, she will reply before lunch.*
watch: *unless* = *if not*: *Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus* (not *Unless you don't hurry*).
*if* (maybe it happens) and *when* (it will happen): *If I see her, I'll tell her. When I see her, I'll tell her.*
No *will* after *if*: *If it rains tomorrow…* (not *If it will rain tomorrow…*).
The comma works the same way as in the zero conditional.

form: *If* + Present Simple, *will* + pamatforma: *If it rains, we will stay home.*
Nosacījuma palīgteikums (*if* daļa) var būt arī otrā vietā: *We will stay home if it rains.*
Rezultātā var lietot arī *may, might, can, should*.
Pēc *if* nelieto *will*: *If it rains* (nevis *If it will rain*).
use: Reālas, iespējamas nākotnes situācijas.
Solījumi, brīdinājumi un piedāvājumi.
First conditional = viena nākotnes situācija. Zero conditional = vienmēr patiesi.
rule_lv.signals: *if, unless, as soon as, when, in case*
watch: *unless = if not*: *Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus* (nevis *Unless you don't hurry*).
*if* (varbūt notiks) un *when* (*noteikti* notiks): *If I see her, I'll tell her.* *When I see her, I'll tell her.*
Aiz *if* nav *will*: *If it rains tomorrow*… (nevis *If it will rain tomorrow*…). *Latviski* ja rīt līs, tāpēc *gribas will*.
*Komats* pēc tā paša *principa* kā *zero conditional*.

form: *If* + past simple, *would* + base verb: *If I won the lottery, I would quit my job.*
Use *were* for every person in careful English: *If I were you, ...*
Question: *What would you do if ...?*
*Could* or *might* can replace *would.*
use: Unreal or unlikely situations in the present or future.
Advice: *If I were you, I'd talk to your manager.*
Imagining.
rule.signals: *if, imagine, suppose, if I were you*
rule.example: *If I were the boss, I would cancel Mondays.*

form: *If* + Past Simple, *would* + pamatforma: *If I won the lottery, I would quit my job.*
Rūpīgā valodā visām personām lieto *were*: *If I were you*, ...
Jautājums: *What would you do if* ...?
*Would* vietā var lietot *could* vai *might*.
use: Nereālas vai maz ticamas situācijas tagadnē vai nākotnē.
Padoms: *If I were you, I'd talk to your manager.*
Iztēle.
rule_lv.signals: *if, imagine, suppose, if I were you*

skills.label: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)

form: *If* + past perfect, *would have* + past participle: *If I had known, I would have called.*
Negative: *If I hadn't ..., I wouldn't have ...*
*Could have* or *might have* if the result is less sure.
use: Unreal situations in the past: it did not happen.
Regret and criticism.
Imagining a different past.
rule.signals: *if, if only, too late, I wish* (past)
rule.example: *If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train.*

form: *If* + Past Perfect, *would have* + 3. forma: *If I had known, I would have called.*
Noliegums: *If I hadn't ..., I wouldn't have* ...
*Could have* vai *might have*, ja rezultāts nav tik drošs.
use: Nereālas situācijas pagātnē: tas nenotika.
Nožēla un kritika.
Iztēle par citādu pagātni.
rule_lv.signals: *if, if only, too late, I wish* (pagātne)

form: Past condition, present result: *If* + past perfect, *would* + base verb: *If I had taken that job, I would be rich now.*
Present condition, past result: *If* + past simple, *would have* + past participle: *If I weren't so shy, I would have asked her.*
use: A past event that changes the present.
A present situation that would have changed a past event.
rule.signals: *now, still, today, by now, at the time*
rule.example: *If I had learned English earlier, I would speak it perfectly now.*

form: Inversion (formal): *Had I known, I would have helped.* = *If I had known.*
*Should you need help, call me.* = *If you should need help.*
*Were she here, she would agree.* = *If she were here.*
*unless* = *if ... not.* *as long as / provided that* = *only if.*
*wish* + past simple (now), *wish* + past perfect (regret), *wish* + *would* (annoyance).
use: Formal writing and speaking.
Strong regret and wishes.
Conditions with *unless, as long as, provided that, otherwise, but for.*
rule.signals: *had I, should you, were I, unless, provided that, as long as, otherwise, I wish, if only*
rule.example: *Had I known about the delay, I would have taken a taxi.*

form: *said / told* + (*that*) + clause: *She said (that) she was tired.*
Tenses usually go one step back: *am/is → was, work → worked, worked → had worked, will → would, can → could.*
Pronouns and time words change: *I → he/she, now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, here → there.*
*tell* needs a person: *He told me.* *say* does not: *He said that ...*
use: Telling someone what another person said.
If the fact is still true, the tense can stay: *She said she is tired.* Going one step back is usual after a past reporting verb, but it is not always needed.
rule.signals: *said, told, now → then, yesterday → the day before*
rule.example: *"I'm working late," he said.* → *He said he was working late.*

form: *said / told* + (*that*) + teikums: *She said* (*that*) *she was tired*.
Laiks parasti iet vienu soli atpakaļ: *am/is → was, work → worked, worked → had worked, will → would, can → could*.
Mainās vietniekvārdi un laika vārdi: *I → he/she, now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, here → there.*
*tell* vajag personu: *He told me.* *say* bez personas: *He said that* ...
use: Pastāstīt, ko cits cilvēks teica.
Ja fakts joprojām ir patiess, laiku var nemainīt: *She said she is tired.* Pēc darbības vārda pagātnē laiku parasti *maina* uz vienu soli atpakaļ, bet *ne* vienmēr.
rule_lv.signals: *said, told, now → then, yesterday → the day before*

form: Yes/no questions: *asked* + *if / whether* + subject + verb: *She asked if I liked coffee.*
Wh-questions: *asked* + question word + subject + verb: *He asked where I lived.*
Statement word order, no *do / does / did* to invert the question: *She asked what I did* (not *what did I do*).
Requests and orders: *told / asked* + person + (*not*) *to* + base verb: *He told me to wait.*
use: Reporting what someone asked: the tense shifts back (*Where do you work?* → *She asked me where I worked*). In indirect questions (*Could you tell me where you work?*) it does not: only the word order changes.
Reporting what someone told or asked you to do.
rule.signals: *asked, wondered, wanted to know, told someone to*
rule.example: *"Where do you work?"* → *She asked me where I worked.*

form: Jā/nē jautājumi: *asked + if / whether* + teik. priekšmets + darbības vārds: *She asked if I liked coffee.*
Jautājumi ar jautājamo vārdu: *asked* + jautājamais vārds + teik. priekšmets + darbības vārds: *He asked where I lived.*
Teikuma vārdu secība, bez *do / does / did* jautājuma secībai: *She asked what I did* (nevis *what did I do*).
Lūgumi un rīkojumi: *told / asked* + persona + (*not*) *to* + pamatforma: *He told me to wait.*
use: Pastāstīt, ko kāds jautāja: laiks pāriet pagātnē (*Where do you work?* → *She asked me where I worked*). Netiešajos jautājumos (*Could you tell me where you work*?) laiks nemainās, mainās *tikai* vārdu secība.
Pastāstīt, ko kāds lika vai lūdza darīt.
rule_lv.signals: *asked, wondered, wanted to know, told someone to*

form: verb + *that*: *admit, claim, complain, explain, insist, promise, warn, announce.*
verb + person + *to* + base verb: *advise, warn, remind, invite, encourage, persuade.*
verb + *to* + base verb: *offer, refuse, promise, threaten, agree.*
verb + -ing: *suggest, admit, deny, recommend.*
verb + preposition + -ing: *apologise for, insist on, accuse (someone) of, congratulate (someone) on.*
use: Reporting what the person meant to do (promise, warn, deny), not only the words.
Shorter and more natural than *said that ...*
rule.signals: *admitted, denied, suggested, insisted, promised, warned, apologised for*
rule.example: *"I'm sorry I'm late."* → *He apologised for being late.*

skills.label: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)

form: Start with: *Could you tell me / Do you know / Can you tell me / I wonder.*
Then use statement word order: *... where the station is* (not *where is the station*).
Do not use *do / does / did* to invert the second part: *... what time the shop opens.*
Yes/no questions: use *if* or *whether*: *Do you know if she is here?*
use: Asking politely: *Could you tell me where ...?* The question is a request.
Talking to strangers, customers and at work.
A full stop after *I wonder ...* / *I'd like to know ...*; a question mark after *Could you* / *Do you know ...*
No tense change: only the word order changes (*Where is the station?* → *Could you tell me where the station is?*). In reported questions the tense shifts back (*She asked where the station was*).
rule.signals: *Could you tell me, Do you know, I wonder, I'd like to know, Would you mind telling me*
rule.example: *Could you tell me where the meeting room is?*

form: Sāc ar: *Could you tell me / Do you know / Can you tell me / I wonder.*
Tad lieto teikuma vārdu secību: ... *where the station is* (nevis *where is the station*).
Palīgteikumā nelieto *do / does / did* jautājuma secībai: ... *what time the shop opens*.
Jā/nē jautājumos lieto *if* vai *whether*: *Do you know if she is here?*
use: Pieklājīgs lūgums: *Could you tell me where* ...? Jautājums ir lūgums.
Sarunā ar svešiem cilvēkiem, klientiem un darbā.
Pēc *I wonder* ... / *I'd like to know* ... liek punktu; pēc *Could you / Do you know* ... jautājuma zīmi.
Laiks nemainās, mainās *tikai* vārdu secība (*Where is the station?* → *Could you tell me where the station is*?). Atstāstītajos jautājumos laiks pāriet pagātnē (*She asked where the station was*).
rule_lv.signals: *Could you tell me, Do you know, I wonder, I'd like to know, Would you mind telling me*

skills.label: Indirect questions, more uses (I don't know what to do)

form: Question word + *to* + base verb: *I don't know what to do. I'm not sure how to start.*
*if / whether* + subject + verb: *I wonder if / whether I should accept.* *whether* + *to* + base verb: *I can't decide whether to accept.*
An embedded question can be a subject: *Whether he will come is still unclear.*
After prepositions: *We talked about how to improve the results.*
use: The same structure as *Could you tell me where ...?*, inside statements and phrases: *I don't know what to do. Whether he will come is still unclear.*
No tense change: only the word order changes. In reported questions the tense shifts back (*She asked what I wanted*).
Reports, emails, formal writing and everyday conversation.
Uncertainty: *no idea, not sure, can't remember, unclear, it depends on.*
rule.signals: *I wonder, no idea, not sure, it depends on, the question is*
rule.example: *I have no idea how long the meeting will take.*

skills.label: Used to and be used to

form: *used to* + base verb: *I used to live in Riga.*
Negative: *didn't use to* + base verb (no *-d*): *She didn't use to like fish.*
Question: *Did* + subject + *use to* + base verb? *Did you use to play tennis?*
*be used to / get used to* + noun or verb-*ing*: *I'm used to getting up early. It took me a month to get used to the cold.*
use: *used to*: a habit or a state in the past that is not true now (*I used to smoke. He used to be shy*).
Not for one finished event: use the Past Simple (*We went to Rome last year*).
*be used to / get used to*: something is (or becomes) normal for you. It is different from *used to*!
rule.signals: *when I was young, as a child, in those days, now, any more*
rule.example: *I used to walk to school, but now I'm used to taking the bus.*

form: *used to* + darbības vārda pamatforma: *I used to live in Riga.*
Noliegums: *didn't use to* + pamatforma (bez *-d*): *She didn't use to like fish.*
Jautājums: *Did* + teik. priekšmets + *use to* + pamatforma? *Did you use to play tennis?*
*be used to / get used to* + lietvārds vai darbības vārds ar *-ing*: *I'm used to getting up early.* *It took me a month to get used to the cold.*
use: *used to*: ieradums vai stāvoklis pagātnē, kas tagad vairs nav spēkā (*I used to smoke.* *He used to be shy*).
Nelieto vienam pabeigtam notikumam: lieto Past Simple (*We went to Rome last year*).
*be used to / get used to*: kaut kas ir (vai kļūst) ierasts. Tas atšķiras no *used to*!
rule_lv.signals: *when I was young, as a child, in those days, now, any more* (kad biju jauns, bērnībā, tolaik, tagad, vairs)

skills.label: Articles: a, an, the, no article

form: *a / an* + singular countable noun: *a book, an apple* (*an* before a vowel sound: *an hour*, *a university*).
*the* + singular, plural or uncountable noun: *the book, the books, the water.*
No article: plural and uncountable nouns in general (*Dogs are friendly. I like coffee*) and most names of people, cities and countries (*Riga, Latvia*).
use: *a / an*: one of many, or the first time we mention something (*I saw a film. It was a comedy*).
*the*: something both people know, something already mentioned, or the only one (*the film we saw, the sun, the Internet*).
*the* is also used with superlatives, rivers, seas and some countries (*the best, the Baltic Sea, the UK*).
No article: general things, meals, and places used for their purpose (*have breakfast, go to school, at work*).
rule.signals: *first mention, already mentioned, the only one, in general*
rule.example: *I bought a jacket and a hat. The jacket was cheap, but I love hats.*
watch: *the* with instruments and some places: *play the piano, go to the cinema, listen to the radio*.

rows: one of many, the first time we mention it, jobs
we both know which one, the second time, the only one
things in general, meals, sports, languages, most names
*a film, an apple, She's a nurse.*
*the film we saw, the sun, the Internet*
*I like coffee. have lunch, play football, Riga*
choice.note: *a / an* by sound: *a university, a European, an hour, an MBA*.

mistakes: I go to work by the bus.
I go to work by bus.

ex: I saw [[a]] dog. [[The]] dog was huge.

uses.t: *the* with the only one, superlatives, seas and rivers, some countries
Places used for their purpose: no article
ex: The children go to [[school]] at eight.

watch: *the* with instruments and some places: *play the piano, go to the cinema, listen to the radio*.

form: *a / an* + vienskaitļa skaitāms lietvārds: *a book, an apple* (*an* pirms patskaņa skaņas: *an hour, a university*).
*the* + vienskaitļa, daudzskaitļa vai neskaitāms lietvārds: *the book, the books, the water*.
Bez artikula: daudzskaitļa un neskaitāmi lietvārdi vispārīgā nozīmē (*Dogs are friendly.* *I like coffee*) un lielākā daļa cilvēku, pilsētu un valstu nosaukumu (*Riga, Latvia*).
use: *a / an*: viens no daudziem vai kaut kas, ko piemin pirmoreiz (*I saw a film.* *It was a comedy*).
*the*: kaut kas, ko abi zina, kas jau minēts vai kas ir vienīgais (*the film we saw, the sun, the Internet*).
*the* lieto arī ar vispārākās pakāpes formu, upēm, jūrām un dažām valstīm (*the best, the Baltic Sea, the UK*).
Bez artikula: vispārīgas lietas, ēdienreizes un vietas ar to parasto nozīmi (*have breakfast, go to school, at work*).
rule_lv.signals: *first mention, already mentioned, the only one, in general* (pirmoreiz, jau minēts, vienīgais, vispārīgi)
watch: Latviešu valodā artikulu nav, tāpēc tos bieži izlaiž, īpaši pie profesijām: *She's [[a]] nurse.*
*the* ar mūzikas instrumentiem un dažām vietām: *play the piano, go to the cinema, listen to the radio*.

rows: viens no daudziem, pieminam pirmo reizi, profesijas
abi zinām, kurš; otro reizi; vienīgais
vispārīgi, ēdienreizes, sports, valodas, vairums vārdu
*a film, an apple, She's a nurse.*
*the film we saw, the sun, the Internet*
*I like coffee. have lunch, play football, Riga*
choice.note: *a / an* pēc skaņas: *a university, a European, an hour, an MBA*.

mistakes: I go to work by the bus.
I go to work by bus.

ex: I saw [[a]] dog. [[The]] dog was huge.

uses.t: *the* ar vienīgo, ar "vis-" (superlatīvu), jūrām un upēm, dažām valstīm
Vietas, ko lieto to nolūkam: bez artikula
ex: The children go to [[school]] at eight.

watch: Latviešu valodā artikulu nav, tāpēc tos bieži izlaiž, īpaši pie profesijām: *She's [[a]] nurse.*
*the* ar mūzikas instrumentiem un dažām vietām: *play the piano, go to the cinema, listen to the radio*.

skills.label: Quantity: some, any, much, many, enough

form: *some / any* + plural or uncountable noun: *some apples, any milk.*
*many* + plural: *many people*. *much* + uncountable: *much time*. Mostly in questions and negatives: *How many? How much? not many, not much.*
*a lot of / lots of* + both, mostly in positive sentences: *a lot of people, a lot of time.*
*a few* + plural: *a few friends*. *a little* + uncountable: *a little time*. *few / little* (without *a*) = almost none.
*enough* + noun: *enough chairs*. Adjective + *enough*: *big enough*. *too much / too many* = more than we need.
use: *some*: positive sentences and offers (*Would you like some tea?*). *any*: questions and negatives (*Do you have any brothers? I don't have any money*).
*a few / a little* = a small number, a positive feeling. *few / little* = almost none, a negative feeling.
*too much / too many* is a problem. *not enough* = less than we need.
rule.signals: *how many, how much, a few, a little, enough, too much, too many*
rule.example: *There isn't much time and there are too many things to do.*
watch: Uncountable + singular verb: *There [[is]] a lot of traffic. The money [[is]] on the table.*
*any* = it doesn't matter which: *Take any seat.*
*no* = *not any*: *There's no milk.* = *There isn't any milk.*
*much* in positive sentences sounds formal: *a lot of time* is more natural.

choice.note: *few / little* without *a* = almost none: *Few people came.* (a negative feeling)

ex: We have [[enough]] chairs. The room is big [[enough]].
There are [[too many]] cars in the city.

watch: Uncountable + singular verb: *There [[is]] a lot of traffic. The money [[is]] on the table.*
*any* = it doesn't matter which: *Take any seat.*
*no* = *not any*: *There's no milk.* = *There isn't any milk.*
*much* in positive sentences sounds formal: *a lot of time* is more natural.

form: *some / any* + daudzskaitļa vai neskaitāms lietvārds: *some apples, any milk*.
*many* + daudzskaitlis: *many people*. *much* + neskaitāms lietvārds: *much time*. Galvenokārt jautājumos un noliegumos: *How many?* *How much?* *not many, not much*.
*a lot of / lots of* + abi veidi, galvenokārt apgalvojumos: *a lot of people, a lot of time*.
*a few* + daudzskaitlis: *a few friends*. *a little* + neskaitāms lietvārds: *a little time*. *few / little* (bez *a*) = gandrīz nav.
*enough* + lietvārds: *enough chairs*. Īpašības vārds + *enough*: *big enough*. *too much / too many* = vairāk, nekā vajag.
use: *some*: apgalvojumos un piedāvājumos (*Would you like some tea*?). *any*: jautājumos un noliegumos (*Do you have any brothers?* *I don't have any money*).
*a few / a little = neliels* daudzums, pozitīvs vērtējums. *few / little* = gandrīz nav, negatīvs vērtējums.
*too much / too many* ir problēma. *not enough* = mazāk, nekā vajag.
rule_lv.signals: *how many, how much, a few, a little, enough, too much, too many* (cik, mazliet, pietiekami, par daudz)
watch: Nesaskaitāms + vienskaitlis: *There [[is]] a lot of traffic. The money [[is]] on the table.* Latviski "nauda ir", bet "mati ir" daudzskaitlī: angliski *hair* ir nesaskaitāms.
*any* = vienalga kurš: *Take any seat.*
*no* = *not any*: *There's no milk.* = *There isn't any milk.*
*much* apstiprinājumā izklausās oficiāli: *a lot of time* ir dabiskāk.

choice.note: *few / little* bez *a* = gandrīz nemaz: *Few people came.* (negatīva nozīme)

ex: We have [[enough]] chairs. The room is big [[enough]].
There are [[too many]] cars in the city.

watch: Nesaskaitāms + vienskaitlis: *There [[is]] a lot of traffic. The money [[is]] on the table.* Latviski "nauda ir", bet "mati ir" daudzskaitlī: angliski *hair* ir nesaskaitāms.
*any* = vienalga kurš: *Take any seat.*
*no* = *not any*: *There's no milk.* = *There isn't any milk.*
*much* apstiprinājumā izklausās oficiāli: *a lot of time* ir dabiskāk.

form: *who* = people, *which* = things, *that* = people or things: *a woman who lives next door, a phone which takes good photos.*
*where* = places, *whose* = belongs to: *the restaurant where we met, a driver whose car was stolen.*
Defining clause: no commas, it tells us which one: *The woman who called is my boss.* *Who / which / that* can be left out when it is the object: *the film we saw.*
Non-defining clause: commas, extra information, not *that*: *My brother, who lives in Berlin, is a nurse.*
use: A relative clause gives more information about a noun and joins two sentences into one.
Defining: we need it to know which person or thing. Non-defining: extra information we could leave out.
Do not repeat the object: *the book that I bought*, not *the book that I bought it.*
rule.signals: *who, which, that, where, whose, commas*
rule.example: *The woman who called is my boss, and the office where she works is in Riga.*

form: *who* = cilvēki, *which* = lietas, *that* = cilvēki vai lietas: *a woman who lives next door, a phone which takes good photos*.
*where* = vietas, *whose* = kam pieder: *the restaurant where we met, a driver whose car was stolen*.
Palīgteikums bez komatiem (vajadzīgs, lai zinātu, kuru): *The woman who called is my boss.* *Who / which / that* var izlaist, ja tas ir papildinātājs: *the film we saw*.
Palīgteikums ar komatiem (papildu informācija), ne *that*: *My brother, who lives in Berlin, is a nurse.*
use: Attieksmes palīgteikums dod vairāk informācijas par lietvārdu un savieno divus teikumus vienā.
Bez komatiem: informācija vajadzīga, lai zinātu, par kuru cilvēku vai lietu runa. Ar komatiem: papildu informācija, ko var izlaist.
Nekad neatkārto papildinātāju: *the book that I bought*, nevis *the book that I bought it*.
rule_lv.signals: *who, which, that, where, whose, commas* (komati)

skills.label: Time clauses (when, as soon as, until)

form: *when / as soon as / until / before / after / while* + Present Simple (not *will*) for the future: *I'll call you when I arrive.*
The time clause can come first (with a comma) or second: *When I arrive, I'll call you.* = *I'll call you when I arrive.*
With *after* and *before* the Present Perfect is also possible: *I'll call you after I've finished.*
use: The main clause has *will / going to* or an order; the time clause has the present.
*when* = at that time. *as soon as* = immediately. *until* = up to that moment (*Wait here until I come back*). *before / after* = which happens first. *while* = at the same time.
rule.signals: *when, as soon as, until, before, after, while, by the time*
rule.example: *I'll tell you the news as soon as I get home.*

form: *when / as soon as / until / before / after / while* + Present Simple (nevis *will*) nākotnei: *I'll call you when I arrive.*
Laika palīgteikums var būt pirmais (ar komatu) vai otrais: *When I arrive, I'll call you.* = *I'll call you when I arrive.*
Ar *after* un *before* iespējams arī Present Perfect: *I'll call you after I've finished.*
use: Virsteikumā ir *will / going to* vai pavēle; laika palīgteikumā ir tagadne.
*when* = tajā laikā. *as soon as* = uzreiz. *until* = līdz tam brīdim (*Wait here until I come back*). *before / after* = kas notiek pirmais. *while* = vienlaikus.
rule_lv.signals: *when, as soon as, until, before, after, while, by the time* (kad, līdzko, līdz, pirms, pēc, kamēr)

form: Positive sentence, negative tag: *You like tea, don't you?*
Negative sentence, positive tag: *She isn't here, is she?*
The tag repeats the auxiliary: *is / are / was / were, have / has, can, will, should*. With the Present Simple and Past Simple: *do / does / did*.
Special: *I am* → *aren't I?* *Let's* → *shall we?* An order → *will you?* *Nobody / nothing* → positive tag with *they / it*.
use: Voice goes down: you are sure and want agreement (*It's cold, isn't it?*).
Voice goes up: you are not sure and really ask (*You're not working today, are you?*).
The tag has the same tense as the sentence: *He went home, didn't he?*
rule.signals: *isn't it? don't you? can't he? will you? aren't I?*
rule.example: *You haven't seen my keys, have you?*

form: Apgalvojošs teikums, nolieguma *tag*: *You like tea, don't you?*
Noliegts teikums, apgalvojošs *tag*: *She isn't here, is she?*
*Tag* atkārto palīgdarbības vārdu: *is / are / was / were, have / has, can, will, should*. Ar Present Simple un Past Simple: *do / does / did*.
Īpašie gadījumi: *I am → aren't I?* *Let's → shall we?* Pavēle → *will you*? *Nobody / nothing* → apgalvojošs *tag* ar *they / it*.
use: Balss krītas: esi pārliecināts un gaidi piekrišanu (*It's cold, isn't it*?).
Balss ceļas: neesi drošs un tiešām jautā (*You're not working today, are you*?).
*Tag* ir tajā pašā laikā kā teikums: *He went home, didn't he?*
rule_lv.signals: *isn't it*? *don't you*? *can't he*? *will you*? *aren't I*? (īss jautājums teikuma beigās)

form: Object question with most main verbs in the present or past simple: question word + *do / does / did* + subject + base verb: *Who did you meet? What does she want?* With another auxiliary or a modal, that word comes first: *What are you doing? Who can you see?*
Neutral subject question: the question word is the subject, no *do / does / did*: *Who met you? What happened? Who wants coffee?* (Only for emphasis: *Who did call?*)
The verb keeps the normal form: *Who lives here?* (with *-s*), not *Who does live here?*
use: Ask about the person or thing that does the action: subject question (*Tom called me → Who called you?*).
Ask about the person or thing the action happens to: object question (*I called Tom → Who did you call?*).
Look at the answer: if the answer is the subject, the neutral question has no *did / does*.
rule.signals: *who, what, which, whose as the subject: no do / does / did*
rule.example: *Who wrote this email? Who did you send it to?*
watch: A preposition often goes at the end: *Who are you talking to? What are you looking at?*
*Which / What / How many* + noun as the subject: no *do*: *Which bus goes to the centre? How many people came?*
*Who* takes a singular verb, even if the answer is two people: *Who lives here? Tom and Anna.*
Questions with *be*: no *do*: *Where is she? Were they late?*
Indirect questions have a different order: *Do you know where she lives?* (a separate topic)

form: Jautājums par papildinātāju ar lielāko daļu darbības vārdu *Present* vai Past Simple: jautājamais vārds + *do / does / did* + teik. priekšmets + pamatforma: *Who did you meet?* *What does she want?* Ar *citu* palīgdarbības vārdu vai modālo vārdu tas ir pirmais: *What are you doing?* *Who can you see?*
Neitrāls jautājums par teikuma priekšmetu: jautājamais vārds pats ir teik. priekšmets, bez *do / does / did*: *Who met you?* *What happened?* *Who wants coffee?* (Tikai *uzsvaram*: *Who did call*?)
Darbības vārds paliek parastajā formā: *Who lives here?* (ar *-s*), nevis *Who does live here?*
use: Jautā par cilvēku vai lietu, kas veic darbību: jautājums par teikuma priekšmetu (*Tom called me → Who called you*?).
Jautā par cilvēku vai lietu, ar ko darbība notiek: jautājums par papildinātāju (*I called Tom → Who did you call*?).
Paskaties uz atbildi: ja atbilde ir teik. priekšmets, neitrālajā jautājumā nav *did / does*.
rule_lv.signals: *who, what, which, whose as the subject*: no *do / does / did* (kā teik. priekšmets: bez *do / does / did*)
watch: Prievārds bieži ir beigās: *Who are you talking to?* *What are you looking at?* *Latviski* prievārds ir sākumā: Ar ko *tu* runā?
*Which / What / How many* + lietvārds kā teikuma priekšmets: bez *do*: *Which bus goes to the centre?* *How many people came?*
*Who* lieto ar *vienskaitli*, arī ja atbilde ir *divi* cilvēki: *Who lives here?* *Tom and Anna.*
Jautājumos ar *be do nevajag*: *Where is she?* *Were they late?*
Netiešajiem jautājumiem ir *cita* secība: *Do you know where she lives?* (atsevišķa tēma)

form: verb + *-ing*: *enjoy, finish, keep, avoid, mind, suggest, practise* (*I enjoy reading. She suggested going home.*)
verb + *to* + base verb: *want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn, agree, promise, manage, refuse* (*I want to leave. He decided to stay.*)
preposition + *-ing*: *interested in learning, good at cooking, before leaving, thank you for helping.*
Some verbs take both with a very similar meaning: *like, love, hate, start, begin* (*I like swimming. ≈ I like to swim.* The emphasis can differ.)
Different meaning: *stop / remember / forget / try* + *-ing* or *to* (*I stopped smoking = I quit. I stopped to smoke = I stopped in order to smoke.*)
use: The verb decides: learn which verbs go with *-ing* and which with *to*.
After a preposition we use *-ing* when a verb follows directly: *She's good at drawing.* (A question word + *to* can also follow: *about how to improve it*.)
*stop / remember / forget / try*: *-ing* = about something done or an experiment; *to* = a task or a purpose.
rule.signals: *enjoy, avoid, finish + -ing; want, decide, hope + to; after a preposition: -ing*
rule.example: *I enjoy cooking, but I decided to eat out tonight.*
watch: *want / would like* + person + *to*: *I want you to come* (not *I want that you come*).
*let / make* + person + base verb: *Let me go. She made me laugh.*
Modal verbs + base verb, without *to*: *I can swim.*
*go* + *-ing* for activities: *go shopping, go swimming*.
*look forward to* + *-ing*: *I look forward to seeing you.*

rows: *enjoy, finish, mind, avoid, suggest, keep, practise*
*want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn, agree, promise, manage, refuse*
*like, love, hate, start, begin* (almost the same meaning)
choice.note: After a preposition: always *-ing*: *good at [[cooking]], before [[leaving]], thank you for [[helping]]*.

ex: I stopped [[to smoke]]. (= to have a cigarette)
Remember [[to call]] her. (a task) / I remember [[meeting]] her. (a memory)

watch: *want / would like* + person + *to*: *I want you to come* (not *I want that you come*).
*let / make* + person + base verb: *Let me go. She made me laugh.*
Modal verbs + base verb, without *to*: *I can swim.*
*go* + *-ing* for activities: *go shopping, go swimming*.
*look forward to* + *-ing*: *I look forward to seeing you.*

form: darbības vārds + *-ing*: *enjoy, finish, keep, avoid, mind, suggest, practise* (*I enjoy reading.* *She suggested going home*.)
darbības vārds + to + pamatforma: *want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn, agree, promise, manage, refuse* (*I want to leave.* *He decided to stay*.)
prievārds + *-ing*: *interested in learning, good at cooking, before leaving, thank you for helping*.
Daži darbības vārdi der ar abiem ar ļoti līdzīgu nozīmi: *like, love, hate, start, begin* (*I like swimming.* ≈ *I like to swim.* *Uzsvars* var atšķirties.)
Atšķirīga nozīme: *stop / remember / forget / try + -ing* vai *to* (*I stopped smoking* = es atmetu. *I stopped to smoke* = es apstājos, lai nosmēķētu.)
use: Darbības vārds nosaka formu: iemācies, kuri vārdi iet ar *-ing* un kuri ar to.
Aiz prievārda lieto *-ing*, ja tieši seko darbības vārds: *She's good at drawing.* (Var *sekot* arī jautājamais vārds + *to*: *about how to improve it*.)
*stop / remember / forget / try*: *-ing* = par jau izdarītu vai izmēģinājumu; to = uzdevums vai mērķis.
rule_lv.signals: *enjoy, avoid, finish + -ing; want, decide, hope + to; after a preposition*: *-ing* (aiz prievārda: *-ing*)
watch: *want / would like* + cilvēks + *to*: *I want you to come* (nevis *I want that you come*). Latviski "gribu, lai tu atnāc", tāpēc rodas *that*.
*let / make* + cilvēks + pamatforma: *Let me go. She made me laugh.*
Modālie darbības vārdi + pamatforma bez *to*: *I can swim.*
*go* + *-ing* nodarbēm: *go shopping, go swimming*.
*look forward to* + *-ing*: *I look forward to seeing you.*

rows: *enjoy, finish, mind, avoid, suggest, keep, practise*
*want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn, agree, promise, manage, refuse*
*like, love, hate, start, begin* (gandrīz tā pati nozīme)
choice.note: Aiz prievārda vienmēr *-ing*: *good at [[cooking]], before [[leaving]], thank you for [[helping]]*.

ex: I stopped [[to smoke]]. (= apstājos, lai uzsmēķētu)
Remember [[to call]] her. (uzdevums) / I remember [[meeting]] her. (atmiņa)

watch: *want / would like* + cilvēks + *to*: *I want you to come* (nevis *I want that you come*). Latviski "gribu, lai tu atnāc", tāpēc rodas *that*.
*let / make* + cilvēks + pamatforma: *Let me go. She made me laugh.*
Modālie darbības vārdi + pamatforma bez *to*: *I can swim.*
*go* + *-ing* nodarbēm: *go shopping, go swimming*.
*look forward to* + *-ing*: *I look forward to seeing you.*

skills.label: More modals: might, could, be able to

form: *might / may / could* + base verb = possible: *It might rain. She may be late. He could be at home.*
Negative: *might not / may not* + base verb: *They might not come.* *can't* = I am sure it is not true.
*be able to* + base verb = *can* in other tenses: *I was able to finish. She will be able to help. I haven't been able to call.*
*could* = ability in general in the past (*I could swim at five*). *was able to* = one success (*I was able to catch the bus*).
*needn't* + base verb = not necessary: *You needn't wait.* *needn't have* + 3. form = I did it, but it was not necessary: *We needn't have hurried.*
*be allowed to* + base verb = permission: *We are allowed to park here. Children weren't allowed to enter.*
use: *might / may / could*: something is possible and we are not sure. *must*: we are sure it is true. *can't*: we are sure it is not true.
*can* has no future or perfect form: use *be able to* (*I'll be able to come on Friday*).
*needn't* (or *don't need to / don't have to*) = not necessary. *mustn't* = not allowed.
*be allowed to* = permission from a rule or a person. *can* is shorter, but it has no past or future form.
rule.signals: *perhaps, maybe, possibly, one time, not necessary, rules, allowed*
rule.example: *It might rain, so you needn't water the plants.*

form: *might / may / could* + pamatforma = iespējams: *It might rain.* *She may be late.* *He could be at home.*
Noliegums: *might not / may not* + pamatforma: *They might not come.* *can't = esmu* pārliecināts, ka tā nav.
*be able to* + pamatforma = *can citos laikos*: *I was able to finish.* *She will be able to help.* *I haven't been able to call.*
*could* = spēja pagātnē vispār (*I could swim at five*). *was able to* = viens panākums (*I was able to catch the bus*).
*needn't* + pamatforma = nav vajadzības: *You needn't wait.* *needn't have* + 3. forma = es to izdarīju, bet nevajadzēja: *We needn't have hurried.*
*be allowed to* + pamatforma = atļauts: *We are allowed to park here.* *Children weren't allowed to enter.*
use: *might / may / could*: kaut kas ir iespējams, bet *neesam* droši. *must*: *esam* pārliecināti, ka tā ir. *can't*: *esam* pārliecināti, ka tā nav.
*can* nav nākotnes un *perfekta* formas: lieto *be able to* (*I'll be able to come on Friday*).
*needn't* (vai *don't need to / don't have to*) = nav nepieciešams. *mustn't = aizliegts*.
*be allowed to* = atļauja no *noteikuma* vai cilvēka. *can* ir īsāks, bet tam nav pagātnes un nākotnes formas.
rule_lv.signals: *perhaps, maybe, possibly, one time, not necessary, rules, allowed* (varbūt, iespējams, vienu *reizi*, nav vajadzības, noteikumi, atļauts)

form: modal + *be* + 3. form: *The report must be finished today. Tickets can be bought online.*
Negative: modal + *not* + *be* + 3. form: *It can't be repaired. Shoes mustn't be worn inside.*
Question: modal + subject + *be* + 3. form? *Can this be done? Should the door be locked?*
Past: modal + *have been* + 3. form: *The window should have been closed. The accident could have been avoided.*
use: We use the passive with a modal for rules, advice, possibility and ability when the doer is not important (*Tickets can be bought online*).
The modal stays the same: *must / should / can / could / might / will / ought to / has to* + *be* + 3. form.
The doer can be added with *by*: *This must be signed by the manager.*
rule.signals: *must be, can be, should be, ought to be, has to be, should have been*
rule.example: *The tickets can be bought online, but they must be paid for today.*

form: modālais darbības vārds + *be* + 3. forma: *The report must be finished today.* *Tickets can be bought online.*
Noliegums: modālais darbības vārds + *not + be* + 3. forma: *It can't be repaired.* *Shoes mustn't be worn inside.*
Jautājums: modālais darbības vārds + teik. priekšmets + *be* + 3. forma? *Can this be done?* *Should the door be locked?*
Pagātne: modālais darbības vārds + *have been* + 3. forma: *The window should have been closed.* *The accident could have been avoided.*
use: Ciešamo kārtu ar modālo darbības vārdu lieto noteikumiem, *padomiem*, iespējai un spējai, kad darītājs nav svarīgs (*Tickets can be bought online*).
Modālais darbības vārds nemainās: *must / should / can / could / might / will / ought to / has to + be* + 3. forma.
Darītāju var *pievienot* ar *by*: *This must be signed by the manager.*
rule_lv.signals: *must be, can be, should be, ought to be, has to be, should have been* (jābūt, var būt, vajadzētu būt)

form: *have* + object + 3. form: *I had my hair cut. She is having her car repaired.*
*get* + object + 3. form is more informal: *We got the windows cleaned.*
Questions and negatives with *do / does / did*: *Do you have your car washed? I didn't have it checked.*
The doer is usually not named; with *by*: *I had my passport checked by the police.*
use: Someone does a service for us (we ask or pay): *I had my laptop fixed* = someone fixed it for me.
Compare: *I cut my hair* = I did it. *I had my hair cut* = a hairdresser did it.
It can also mean something bad happens to us: *He had his wallet stolen.*
Common services: haircut, car repair, photo, dentist, delivery, painting, cleaning.
rule.signals: *have / get something done, hairdresser, mechanic, dentist, repaired, cut*
rule.example: *We had the kitchen painted last month, and next week we're getting the roof repaired.*

form: *have* + papildinātājs + 3. forma: *I had my hair cut.* *She is having her car repaired.*
*get* + papildinātājs + 3. forma ir sarunvalodā: *We got the windows cleaned.*
Jautājumi un *noliegumi* ar *do / does / did*: *Do you have your car washed?* *I didn't have it checked.*
Darītāju parasti nenosauc; ar *by*: *I had my passport checked by the police.*
use: Kāds *mums* veic *pakalpojumu* (mēs lūdzam vai maksājam): *I had my laptop fixed* = kāds man *to salaboja*.
Salīdzini: *I cut my hair* = es pats to izdarīju. *I had my hair cut = frizieris to* izdarīja.
Tas var nozīmēt arī nepatīkamu *notikumu*: *He had his wallet stolen.*
Biežākie *pakalpojumi*: *matu* griešana, *auto remonts*, fotogrāfija, zobārsts, piegāde, krāsošana, tīrīšana.
rule_lv.signals: *have / get something done, hairdresser, mechanic, dentist, repaired, cut* (*frizieris*, mehāniķis, zobārsts, *salabots, apgriezts*)

skills.label: Verbs with two objects (give me, tell her)

form: verb + person + thing: *She gave me a present. He sent his mother a letter.*
verb + thing + *to / for* + person: *She gave a present to me. He bought a gift for his mother.*
*to*: give, send, show, tell, lend, offer, pay, teach, write, bring. *for*: buy, make, cook, find, get, keep, save.
When the thing is a pronoun, use *to / for*: *Show it to me.* (not *Show me it*)
use: Both patterns have the same meaning. We often put the person first (*She told me a story*) and use *to / for* when the thing is more important.
*explain, suggest, describe, introduce*: always the thing first: *She explained the problem to me.* (not *She explained me the problem*)
rule.signals: *give, send, show, tell, lend, buy, make, to, for*
rule.example: *I bought my sister a book, and I gave it to her yesterday.*
watch: *explain, suggest, describe* with *to*: *Explain it to me* (not *Explain me it*).
*say* with *to*, *tell* without *to*: *She said to me… / She told me…* (not *She said me*).
Two pronouns: *Give it to me* (*Give me it* is heard in speech, but not used in tests).
*for* when we do something to help someone: *I cooked dinner for you.*

form: darbības vārds + cilvēks + *lieta*: *She gave me a present.* *He sent his mother a letter.*
darbības vārds + *lieta + to / for* + cilvēks: *She gave a present to me.* *He bought a gift for his mother.*
*to*: *give, send, show, tell, lend, offer, pay, teach, write, bring*. *for*: *buy, make, cook, find, get, keep, save*.
Ja *lieta* ir vietniekvārds, lieto *to / for*: *Show it to me.* (nevis *Show me it*)
use: Abām konstrukcijām ir viena nozīme. Bieži cilvēku liek *pirmo* (*She told me a story*) un lieto *to / for*, kad *lieta* ir svarīgāka.
*explain, suggest, describe, introduce*: vienmēr *vispirms lieta*: *She explained the problem to me.* (nevis *She explained me the problem*)
rule_lv.signals: *give, send, show, tell, lend, buy, make, to, for* (*dot*, sūtīt, parādīt, pastāstīt, *aizdot, pirkt*, taisīt)
watch: *explain, suggest, describe* lieto ar *to*: *Explain it to me* (nevis *Explain me it*). *Latviski paskaidro* man, tāpēc *gribas likt* cilvēku *pirmo*.
*say* lieto ar *to, tell* bez *to*: *She said to me*… / *She told me*… (nevis *She said me*).
*Divi* vietniekvārdi: *Give it to me* (*Give me it* bieži *dzird* sarunā, bet *testos* nelieto).
*for* lieto, kad dara kāda labā: *I cooked dinner for you.*

form: *-ing* adjective: the thing or person that causes the feeling: *a boring film, an interesting book, a tiring day.*
*-ed* adjective: the person who has the feeling: *I am bored. She was interested. We felt tired.*
Pairs: *bored / boring, interested / interesting, excited / exciting, tired / tiring, surprised / surprising, annoyed / annoying, confused / confusing.*
use: *The film was boring* (it causes the feeling). *The audience was bored* (they have the feeling).
A person can cause the feeling too: *He is boring* (he makes others bored). *He is bored* (he feels bored).
After *be / feel / look / seem*: *She looks tired* (she is tired). *The lesson is tiring* (it makes us tired).
rule.signals: *feel, felt, seem, a film, a lesson, a story, a day*
rule.example: *I was so bored because the film was really boring.*

form: *-ing* īpašības vārds: *lieta* vai cilvēks, kas *izraisa* sajūtu: *a boring film, an interesting book, a tiring day*.
*-ed* īpašības vārds: cilvēks, *kuram* ir šī sajūta: *I am bored.* *She was interested.* *We felt tired.*
Pāri: *bored / boring, interested / interesting, excited / exciting, tired / tiring, surprised / surprising, annoyed / annoying, confused / confusing*.
use: *The film was boring* (tā *izraisa* sajūtu). *The audience was bored* (cilvēkiem ir šī sajūta).
Sajūtu var izraisīt arī cilvēks: *He is boring* (viņš *citiem* liek *garlaikoties*). *He is bored* (viņam ir garlaicīgi).
Aiz *be / feel / look / seem*: *She looks tired* (viņa ir *noguruse*). *The lesson is tiring* (tā *nogurdina*).
rule_lv.signals: *feel, felt, seem, a film, a lesson, a story, a day* (*just*, šķist, *filma, stunda*, stāsts, *diena*)

form: Opinion before fact: *a lovely old house* (not *an old lovely house*).
Order of facts: size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, then the noun: *a small old round red Italian wooden table.*
Before a noun we usually use two or three adjectives. After *be* we can use *and*: *The room is big, bright and cheap.*
Adjectives have no plural form: *two small boxes* (not *two smalls boxes*).
use: Remember: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, noun.
*a big red Spanish car* sounds natural. *a Spanish red big car* does not.
rule.signals: *opinion, size, age, colour, origin, material*
rule.example: *She bought a beautiful small black leather bag.*

form: *Vispirms viedoklis*, pēc tam fakti: *a lovely old house* (nevis *an old lovely house*).
*Faktu* secība: izmērs, *vecums*, forma, krāsa, *izcelsme*, materiāls, tad lietvārds: *a small old round red Italian wooden table*.
Pirms lietvārda parasti lieto divus vai trīs īpašības vārdus. Aiz *be* var lietot *and*: *The room is big, bright and cheap.*
Īpašības vārdiem nav daudzskaitļa formas: *two small boxes* (nevis *two smalls boxes*).
use: *Atceries*: *viedoklis*, izmērs, *vecums*, forma, krāsa, *izcelsme*, materiāls, lietvārds.
*a big red Spanish car* skan *dabiski*. *a Spanish red big car neskan*.
rule_lv.signals: *opinion, size, age, colour, origin, material* (*viedoklis*, izmērs, *vecums*, krāsa, *izcelsme*, materiāls)

form: Manner: adjective + *-ly*: *slow - slowly, careful - carefully, easy - easily, happy - happily.* Irregular: *good - well, fast - fast, hard - hard, late - late.*
Frequency: *always, usually, often, sometimes, never*. Before the main verb, after *be*: *She often walks. He is always late.*
Degree: *very, really, quite, extremely, too* + adjective or adverb: *very quickly, quite cold.* *enough* comes after the adjective: *warm enough.*
Position: manner adverbs go after the verb or the object: *She speaks English well. He drove the car carefully.*
use: Adjectives describe nouns (*a quick answer*). Adverbs describe verbs, adjectives and other adverbs (*She answered quickly*).
After *be, look, feel, seem, sound* we use an adjective: *She looks happy.* (not *happily*)
*hard* = with effort (*work hard*), *hardly* = almost not (*I can hardly see*). *late* = not on time, *lately* = recently.
Extreme adjectives (*perfect, amazing, exhausted*) take *absolutely / completely*, not *very*.
rule.signals: *-ly, always, never, very, quite, too, enough, absolutely*
rule.example: *He drives carefully, and he never drives too fast.*
watch: *fast, hard, late* have no *-ly*: *He drives fast.*
*hard* = with effort, *hardly* = almost not; *late* = not on time, *lately* = recently.
With two verbs, frequency goes after the first: *I have never been there. She can always help.*

rows: after the verb or the object: *She speaks English well.*
before the main verb, after *be*: *She often walks. He is always late.*
before an adjective or adverb: *very quickly*; *enough* after: *warm enough*

uses.t: Adjective for a noun, adverb for a verb
After *be, look, feel, seem, sound*: an adjective

watch: *fast, hard, late* have no *-ly*: *He drives fast.*
*hard* = with effort, *hardly* = almost not; *late* = not on time, *lately* = recently.
With two verbs, frequency goes after the first: *I have never been there. She can always help.*

form: *Veids*: īpašības vārds + *-ly*: *slow - slowly, careful - carefully, easy - easily, happy - happily*. Neregulāri: *good - well, fast - fast, hard - hard, late - late*.
Biežums: *always, usually, often, sometimes, never*. Pirms darbības vārda, aiz *be*: *She often walks.* *He is always late.*
Pakāpe: *very, really, quite, extremely, too* + īpašības vārds vai apstākļa vārds: *very quickly, quite cold*. *enough* ir aiz īpašības vārda: *warm enough*.
*Vieta* teikumā: *veida* apstākļa vārds ir aiz darbības vārda vai papildinātāja: *She speaks English well.* *He drove the car carefully.*
use: Īpašības vārdi apraksta lietvārdus (*a quick answer*). Apstākļa vārdi apraksta darbības vārdus, īpašības vārdus un *citus* apstākļa vārdus (*She answered quickly*).
Aiz *be, look, feel, seem, sound* lieto īpašības vārdu: *She looks happy.* (nevis *happily*)
*hard* = ar pūlēm (*work hard*), *hardly* = gandrīz nē (*I can hardly see*). *late* = novēloti, *lately = nesen*.
Ar galējiem īpašības vārdiem (*perfect, amazing, exhausted*) lieto *absolutely / completely*, nevis *very*.
rule_lv.signals: *-ly, always, never, very, quite, too, enough, absolutely* (vienmēr, nekad, ļoti, *diezgan*, pārāk, pietiekami)
watch: *fast, hard, late* ir bez *-ly*: *He drives fast.*
*hard* = ar piepūli, *hardly* = gandrīz nemaz; *late* = vēlu, *lately* = pēdējā laikā.
Ja ir divi darbības vārdi, biežums ir aiz pirmā: *I have never been there. She can always help.* Latviski vārdu secība ir brīvāka.

rows: īpašības vārds + *-ly*: *slow → slowly, easy → easily*; *good → well*
aiz darbības vārda vai papildinātāja: *She speaks English well.*
pirms pamatdarbības vārda, aiz *be*: *She often walks. He is always late.*
pirms īpašības vai apstākļa vārda: *very quickly*; *enough* aiz tā: *warm enough*

uses.t: Īpašības vārds lietvārdam, apstākļa vārds darbības vārdam
Aiz *be, look, feel, seem, sound*: īpašības vārds

watch: *fast, hard, late* ir bez *-ly*: *He drives fast.*
*hard* = ar piepūli, *hardly* = gandrīz nemaz; *late* = vēlu, *lately* = pēdējā laikā.
Ja ir divi darbības vārdi, biežums ir aiz pirmā: *I have never been there. She can always help.* Latviski vārdu secība ir brīvāka.

form: *so* + adjective or adverb: *The film was so long. He runs so fast.*
*such* + (*a / an*) + (adjective) + noun: *It was such a long film. They are such nice people.*
*so much / so many* + noun: *so much noise, so many people.*
Result: *so / such ... that*: *It was so cold that we stayed inside. It was such a cold day that we stayed inside.*
use: *so* goes before an adjective or adverb with no noun; *such* goes before a noun (with or without an adjective).
*such* + plural or uncountable noun has no *a / an*: *such good friends, such bad weather.*
*so / such ... that* tells us the result.
rule.signals: *so, such, so much, so many, that (result)*
rule.example: *It was such a cold day that we stayed in, and we were so tired.*

form: *so* + īpašības vārds vai apstākļa vārds: *The film was so long.* *He runs so fast.*
*such* + (*a / an*) + (īpašības vārds) + lietvārds: *It was such a long film.* *They are such nice people.*
*so much / so many* + lietvārds: *so much noise, so many people*.
*Sekas*: *so / such* ... *that*: *It was so cold that we stayed inside.* *It was such a cold day that we stayed inside.*
use: *so* lieto pirms īpašības vārda vai apstākļa vārda bez lietvārda; *such* — pirms lietvārda (ar īpašības vārdu vai bez tā).
*such* + daudzskaitlis vai neskaitāms lietvārds bez *a / an*: *such good friends, such bad weather*.
*so / such* ... *that* parāda *sekas*.
rule_lv.signals: *so, such, so much, so many, that* (*result*) (tik, tāds, tik daudz, ka)

form: *some-* (positive): *someone, somebody, something, somewhere.* *any-* (questions and negatives): *anyone, anybody, anything, anywhere.* *no-*: *no one, nobody, nothing, nowhere.* *every-*: *everyone, everybody, everything, everywhere.*
They take a singular verb: *Everyone is here. Nothing has changed.*
With a negative verb we use *any-*, not *no-*: *I don't know anything.* (not *I don't know nothing*)
Offers and requests: *Would you like something to drink?* (*some-*). Questions: *Is there anyone here?*
We use *they / their* for *somebody, anybody, everybody, nobody*: *Everybody did their best.*
use: *some-* when we expect yes (offers, requests) or the thing exists; *any-* in questions and negatives or when it does not matter (*Anyone can join*).
*no-* already makes the sentence negative: no double negative.
*everyone / everybody* = all the people; *every one* = each single one of a group.
rule.signals: *someone, anything, nobody, everything, anywhere, nowhere*
rule.example: *Everybody was there, but nobody said anything.*

form: *some*- (apgalvojumos): *someone, somebody, something, somewhere*. *any*- (jautājumos un noliegumos): *anyone, anybody, anything, anywhere*. no-: no *one, nobody, nothing, nowhere*. *every*-: *everyone, everybody, everything, everywhere*.
Tiem seko vienskaitļa darbības vārds: *Everyone is here.* *Nothing has changed.*
Ar *noliegtu* darbības vārdu lieto *any*-, nevis no-: *I don't know anything.* (nevis *I don't know nothing*)
Piedāvājumos un lūgumos: *Would you like something to drink?* (*some*-). Jautājumos: *Is there anyone here?*
Ar *somebody, anybody, everybody, nobody* lieto *they / their*: *Everybody did their best.*
use: *some*- lieto, kad gaidām atbildi jā (piedāvājumi, lūgumi) vai kad kaut kas pastāv; *any*- jautājumos un noliegumos vai kad nav svarīgi (*Anyone can join*).
no- jau veido noliegumu: dubultā noliegumu nelieto.
*everyone / everybody = visi* cilvēki; *every one = katrs* atsevišķi no *grupas*.
rule_lv.signals: *someone, anything, nobody, everything, anywhere, nowhere* (kāds, kaut kas, *neviens, viss*, kaut *kur, nekur*)

skills.label: Prepositions after words (listen to, good at)

form: Some words always go with the same preposition. Learn them in pairs: *listen to, wait for, look at, talk to, ask for, pay for, belong to, depend on, think about.*
Adjectives too: *good at, afraid of, interested in, proud of, different from.*
Some verbs take no preposition: *call me, help me, meet you, join the team, answer the question.*
use: After the preposition comes a noun or a pronoun: *Listen to me. I'm waiting for the bus.*
In a question the preposition often goes to the end: *What are you looking at? Who are you waiting for?*
rule.signals: *listen to music, wait for the bus, good at maths, call me*
rule.example: *I'm waiting for Anna. She's good at maths, but she's afraid of dogs.*
watch: Some verbs take no preposition: *discuss the plan* (not *discuss about*), *enter the room* (not *enter into*), *call me* (not *call to me*).
*married to* (not *married with*).
*depend on* (not *depend from*).
After a preposition, a verb takes *-ing*: *good at swimming, interested in learning.*
*arrive in / at*, never *arrive to* (see *In, on, at*).

form: Daži vārdi vienmēr iet kopā ar savu prievārdu. *Tos* mācās *pa* pāriem: *listen to, wait for, look at, talk to, ask for, pay for, belong to, depend on, think about*.
Arī īpašības vārdi: *good at, afraid of, interested in, proud of, different from*.
Daži darbības vārdi ir bez prievārda: *call me, help me, meet you, join the team, answer the question*.
use: Aiz prievārda ir lietvārds vai vietniekvārds: *Listen to me.* *I'm waiting for the bus.*
Jautājumā prievārds bieži ir beigās: *What are you looking at?* *Who are you waiting for?*
rule_lv.signals: *listen to music, wait for the bus, good at maths, call me* (klausīties mūziku, gaidīt *autobusu*, viņai *padodas* matemātika, *piezvani* man)
watch: Daži darbības vārdi ir bez prievārda: *discuss the plan* (nevis *discuss about*), *enter the room* (nevis *enter into*), *call me* (nevis *call to me*). *Latviski apspriest* par, zvanīt kādam, tāpēc *rodas lieks* prievārds.
*married to* (nevis *married with*). *Latviski* precējies ar, tāpēc *rodas with*.
*depend on* (nevis *depend from*). *Latviski* atkarīgs no, tāpēc *rodas from*.
Aiz prievārda darbības vārds ir ar *-ing*: *good at swimming, interested in learning*.
*arrive in / at*, nekad *arrive to* (*sk*. *In / on / at*).

skills.label: Subject and verb (my friend lives, my friends live)

form: One person or thing + verb-*s*: *My friend lives in Riga.*
More than one + verb: *My friends live in Riga.*
One: *is / was / has / does*. More: *are / were / have / do*. *She has a car. They have two.*
use: *and* makes more than one: *Tom and Anna live here.*
*everybody, nobody, something, everyone* + verb-*s*: *Everybody knows. Nothing works.*
rule.signals: *he, she, it, everybody, nobody, every, one of, and, there is / there are*
rule.example: *Everybody in my family likes coffee, but my parents drink tea.*
watch: *people, police, children* are plural: *People [[are]] friendly.*
*news* takes a singular verb: *The news [[is]] good.*
*there is* + one, *there are* + more: *There [[are]] two cafés here.*

mistakes: My sister work in a bank.
My sister works in a bank.

uses.t: The verb agrees with the main noun, not the one next to it
ex: One of my friends [[lives]] in Oslo.
The people in this office [[are]] nice.

watch: *people, police, children* are plural: *People [[are]] friendly.*
*news* takes a singular verb: *The news [[is]] good.*
*there is* + one, *there are* + more: *There [[are]] two cafés here.*

form: Viens cilvēks vai *lieta* + darbības vārds ar *-s*: *My friend lives in Riga.*
Vairāki + darbības vārds bez *-s*: *My friends live in Riga.*
Vienam: *is / was / has / does*. Vairākiem: *are / were / have / do*. *She has a car.* *They have two.*
use: *Latviski draugs* dzīvo un *draugi* dzīvo: forma ir viena. *Angliski* tā mainās: *lives / live*.
*and* nozīmē vairākus: *Tom and Anna live here.* *everybody, nobody, something, everyone* lieto ar *-s*: *Everybody knows.*
rule_lv.signals: *he, she, it, everybody, nobody, every, one of, and, there is / there are* (viņš, viņa, *visi, neviens, katrs*, viens no, un, ir)
watch: *people, police, children* ir daudzskaitlī: *People [[are]] friendly.*
*news* lieto ar vienskaitli: *The news [[is]] good.* Latviski "ziņas" ir daudzskaitlī, tāpēc gribas *are*.
*there is* + viens, *there are* + vairāki: *There [[are]] two cafés here.*

mistakes: My sister work in a bank.
My sister works in a bank.

uses.t: *everybody, nobody, something, every* + darbības vārds ar -s
Darbības vārds saskan ar galveno lietvārdu, nevis ar tuvāko
ex: One of my friends [[lives]] in Oslo.
The people in this office [[are]] nice.

watch: *people, police, children* ir daudzskaitlī: *People [[are]] friendly.*
*news* lieto ar vienskaitli: *The news [[is]] good.* Latviski "ziņas" ir daudzskaitlī, tāpēc gribas *are*.
*there is* + viens, *there are* + vairāki: *There [[are]] two cafés here.*

form: Most nouns add *-s*: *a book, two books*. These change: *child → children, person → people, man → men, woman → women, tooth → teeth, foot → feet, mouse → mice.*
No extra *-s*: *children*, not *childrens*; *teeth*, not *tooths*.
*police* has no *-s*, but it is always plural: *The police are here.*
use: These words take a plural verb: *The children are tired. People like it. My feet hurt.*
rule.signals: *child, person, man, woman, tooth, foot, mouse, police*
rule.example: *One mouse is cute, but ten mice are a problem!*
watch: Vowel + *-y* just adds *-s*: *day → days, boy → boys*.
No plural (uncountable): *advice, information, furniture, news*: *some advice* (not *advices*).

uses.t: These words take a plural verb
Always plural: things with two parts

watch: Vowel + *-y* just adds *-s*: *day → days, boy → boys*.
No plural (uncountable): *advice, information, furniture, news*: *some advice* (not *advices*).

form: Lielākajai daļai lietvārdu pievieno *-s*: *a book, two books*. Šie mainās: *child → children, person → people*, man → *men, woman → women, tooth → teeth, foot → feet, mouse → mice*.
Bez papildu *-s*: *children*, nevis *childrens; teeth*, nevis *tooths*.
*police* ir bez *-s*, bet vienmēr daudzskaitlī: *The police are here.*
use: Ar šiem vārdiem lieto daudzskaitļa darbības vārdu: *The children are tired.* *People like it.* *My feet hurt.*
rule_lv.signals: *child, person*, man, *woman, tooth, foot, mouse, police* (bērns, cilvēks, vīrietis, *sieviete, zobs*, pēda, *pele, policija*)
watch: Patskanis + *-y*: tikai *-s*: *day → days, boy → boys*.
Bez daudzskaitļa: *advice, information, furniture, news*: *some advice* (nevis *advices*). Latviski "padomi, mēbeles, ziņas" ir daudzskaitlī, angliski nē.

uses.t: Šie vārdi ir ar daudzskaitļa darbības vārdu
Vienmēr daudzskaitlī: lietas no divām daļām

skills.label: Prepositions of time and place (in, on, at)

form: Time: *at* + clock time (*at 7*), *on* + day or date (*on Monday, on 5 May*), *in* + month, year, season or part of the day (*in May, in 2020, in winter, in the morning*). But *at night*.
No preposition before *tomorrow, yesterday* and *next / last / this / every* + time: *See you next Monday.*

Place: *at* + a point or a place where you do something (*at the bus stop, at work, at home*), *in* + inside or an area (*in the fridge, in my bag, in Riga*), *on* + a surface (*on the table, on the wall, on the third floor*).
use: Ask: is it a clock time, a day or a longer period? Is it a point, inside something, or on a surface?
rule.signals: *at 7, on Monday, in May, at night, at work, in the kitchen, on the wall*
rule.example: *I start work at 9 on Mondays, but in summer I work from home.*
watch: *in the morning*, but *on Monday morning, on Friday evening*.
*at the weekend* (British), *on the weekend* (American).
*at home, at work, at school*, but *in the house, in the office*.
*on the bus / train / plane*, but *in a car / taxi*.
*arrive in* + a city or country, *arrive at* + a place, never *arrive to*: *We arrived in Riga. We arrived at the station.*

rows: days and dates: *on Monday, on 5 May, on Friday evening*
months, years, seasons, parts of the day: *in May, in 2020, in winter, in the morning*

a surface: *on the table, on the wall, on the third floor*
inside, a town or a country: *in the fridge, in my bag, in Riga*
choice.note: No preposition: *tomorrow, yesterday, next Monday, last week, this year, every day*.

mistakes: The keys are at the table.
The keys are on the table.

form: Laiks: *at* + pulksteņa laiks (*at 7*), *on + diena* vai *datums* (*on Monday, on 5 May*), *in* + mēnesis, *gads, gadalaiks* vai *dienas* daļa (*in May, in 2020, in winter, in the morning*). Bet *at night*.

FINISHED-TIME.name: finished time: past simple, not have done

BACKGROUND.name: in progress at a past moment: was / were doing

TIME-CLAUSE.name: no will after when / if / as soon as

FUTURE.name: future: will / going to, not the present simple

BACKSHIFT.name: reported speech: the tense goes back

COULD.name: could / was able to / managed to

Q-ORDER.name: statement order inside a question (where the station is)

AGREE.name: the verb agrees with the subject

REL-ORDER.name: preposition at the end of a relative clause

REL-WHICH.name: , which for extra information and for a whole idea

IT-THERE.name: It's cold / There is a park

ADV-PLACE.name: always / never before the verb, after be

ARTICLE.name: a / the / my before a noun

THE.name: the or no article (life, the sun)

IRR-PLURAL.name: children, people, teeth, feet, mice, police

DEP-PREP.name: the preposition after a word (depend on, listen to)

PREP-TP.name: in / on / at for time and place, none before next / last / tomorrow

TWO-OBJ.name: explain it to me, introduce you to

COMPARE.name: cheaper / the same as / as ... as
